meta.title: The Crow and the Pitcher
meta.textType: story: a traditional tale told by Grandma

paragraphs: On Saturday, November twenty-first, Dad drove Lily, Tom, and Pip to Green Hill. Grandpa took Dad to see the garden. Grandma brought three glasses of cold water and a red bowl for Pip. It was a hot afternoon, and the children sat on the porch steps after lunch. Grandma sat on a chair and looked at the glasses. "If you put stones in a glass of water, what will happen?" she asked. "The water will go up," said Tom. "Perhaps it will run over," said Lily. "Listen to a story first," said Grandma, "and then you will know."

Grandma began the tale of "The Crow and the Pitcher." A thirsty crow searched for water in a hot field. There was no stream, and there was no pond. At last the crow landed on a table. It saw a tall clay pitcher. The pitcher was nearly empty, and there was water only at the bottom. "Oh dear!" said the crow. "My beak is too short, and I cannot reach the water." The crow tried again and again, but it was impossible.

Then the crow stopped and thought hard. "If I push the pitcher over, the water will run away," it thought. "Then I will have no water at all." Next to the table, the crow saw some small stones. It picked up a stone and dropped it into the pitcher. Then it dropped another stone, and another. The stones began to fill the pitcher. The water rose a little with every stone. The work was hard. However, the crow did not give up. Soon the pitcher was nearly full, and the crow was able to reach the water.

The crow drank the cool water, and its plan was a success. Grandma smiled and stopped. "A clever idea can solve a problem," she said. "Can a crow really think like that?" asked Tom. "I don't believe it." "Crows are clever birds," said Grandma, "so please believe me." "I will try it with my glass," said Tom.

Tom ran to the garden and came back with a few pebbles. He knelt at a low table and dropped a pebble into his glass. The water rose a little. "If I add more pebbles, the water will come up to the top," he said. "Not too many!" said Lily. "If you add too many, the water will run over." Tom dropped one more pebble. The water stopped near the top of the glass. Pip walked to his red bowl and drank. "Pip does not need an idea," said Grandma, "because his bowl is full."
text.summary: Grandma asks a question about stones and water, and then she tells the old tale of a thirsty crow. The crow drops stones into a pitcher until it can drink, and Tom tries the same idea with a glass.
